rationale: Walking trajectories differed across older adults undertaking exercise and Friedreich ataxia cohorts. The Huntington total motor comparison adds an uncertain result and supplies no gait estimate. Parkinson walking speed after cold-pressed safflower remains unmeasured.

The 1982 ataxia crossover reports a small timed-speech gain. Baylor singer trials measured acoustic range and self-perception, and Huntington and ALS publications report totals that include speech items. No result evaluates Parkinson speech intelligibility with verified cold-pressed oil.

Whole-oil rodent movement measures varied by novelty and training. One Huntington total motor score includes bradykinesia without separate changes. Parkinson models using a flavonoid extract address a different preparation.

A randomized Huntington comparator study collected a psychiatric scale with an apathy item but published aggregate interpretation only. Earlier exploratory and depression-like findings are indirect. Cold-pressed oil and Parkinson apathy remain unresolved.

Baylor singer reflux scores contain a swallowing item and a safflower ALS comparator reports bulbar-containing composite scores. The public papers provide no separate swallowing change or cold-pressed Parkinson result.

Friedreich ataxia static balance was largely unchanged and older adults reached a test ceiling. Huntington combined scores obscure the tandem gait and pull test items. Reactive Parkinson balance after cold-pressed oil remains open.

The Huntington motor examination includes arm rigidity, but its study reports total assessment only. Earlier strength and movement findings concern different measures, formulations or disorders. Cold-pressed oil and Parkinson rigidity remain unresolved.

A Friedreich ataxia registry reported five falls on USP oil and seven on active RT001. The European Huntington results omit fall-event details. No PD fall frequency with confirmed cold-pressed oil is available.
